items.evidence: All 24 block sign models in the vanilla 1.21.7 client jar are particle-only (no elements, no parent); vanilla draws the board in SignRenderer/HangingSignRenderer (javap: getSignModel/getSignMaterial/createSignModel). The port's block_entity_render.rs:366 assumes 'the boards are block models' and Kind::Sign carries text only — no board is ever submitted. Same wrong assumption at block_entity_render.rs:1010 and block_entity_cem.rs:11. The 1.21.11 sign-boards fix (ac8dd9dc) does not apply to 1.21.7 as-is. Sign ITEMS are unaffected (flat sprites in vanilla too).
items.title: Sign boards are not rendered: placed signs show floating text only

items.evidence: audio_harness.require_sounds() exits unless .local/horizon-client/1.21.7/assets/minecraft/sounds.json exists; the file is absent from the VM's prepared .local (no assets/ dir at all), from mob-spawn/resources (assets/minecraft/ holds only textures/), and from the client jar (sounds.json ships only in the asset index) — VM-wide search found no copy. Root cause is prepare: --prepare runs optional_imports (panorama/fonts/packs/languages) but sounds need the separate 'horizon-prepare sounds' step or --complete, and prepare-1.21.7.bat runs --prepare only — the laptop's .local almost certainly lacks it too, so the owner's game is very likely silent (verify on the laptop). Runtime: SoundRegistry::load silently skips a missing sounds.json, so every event resolves to Sound::empty(). Blocks sound_event, ambient_sound, music, situational_music, sound_engine, audio_attributes. The wiring spec itself is clean (1,727 sounds.json events vs 1,728 registry events; only the intentional_empty sentinel lacks an entry).
items.title: No sounds.json in the prepared 1.21.7 resources: the game is silent and 6 audio drivers cannot run

items.evidence: Placed: vanilla 1.21.7 models/block/bed.json is particle-only (no elements) and every bed blockstate points at it; BedRenderer draws the whole bed. The port has no Bed kind in block_entity_render.rs and no bed drawing code anywhere (only sleep mechanics in bed_geometry.rs / game/beds.rs), so the mesher emits nothing. Items: vanilla renders all 16 bed items via BedSpecialRenderer (items/red_bed.json: minecraft:special, model {type: minecraft:bed}); the port's SpecialModel::decode has no minecraft:bed arm and the error propagates (item_model.rs:550-554), so all 16 bed items fail ClientItem decode. The 1.21.11 sign-boards fix does NOT cover beds.
items.title: Beds are invisible when placed, and bed items fail to decode

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.7 registers 25 BE renderers; the port's Kind covers 13 plus beacon beams. Missing with visible effect: mob/trial spawner spinning mob (+ trial items) — cage is a block model, the mob is BE-rendered; campfire cooking items (logs are a block model, items are BE-rendered); moving piston — moving_piston's block model is EMPTY, PistonHeadRenderer draws the moving block, so it vanishes mid-stroke; brushable-block brushed item; vault display item (vault.rs is server-tick logic only). Structure-block and test-instance-block renderers are also absent but their visible in-play output is unverified (both have cube block models) — noted, not claimed.
items.title: Five more vanilla block-entity renderers have no port equivalent

items.evidence: Batch 0's FirstPerson repair (9dc5dc8d) dropped the swap-ticker columns — 1.21.7 has no itemSwapTicker/getItemSwapScale (swap animation lives in ItemInHandRenderer hand heights); the repaired oracle's tick line has 20 fields. systemic_note: Two systemic patterns. (1) 'The boards/beds are block models' — the port assumes block-entity geometry lives in block models for signs and beds, but vanilla 1.21.7 renders both entirely in BE renderers (their block models are particle-only); the same wrong assumption also strands the spawner mob, campfire items, moving piston, brushable item and vault item. The block_entity_render driver would catch all of it, but its oracle + ParityFont don't compile. (2) The sound stack is blocked on data, not code: sounds.json was never imported for 1.21.7 (prepare runs --prepare only, never the sounds step), so the game is likely silent on the laptop and all 6 audio_harness drivers gate-fail before any comparison — one 'horizon-prepare sounds' run unblocks both. The wiring spec itself is clean (1,727/1,727 real events).
